title: A HARPS wave at 22.9 days does not reduce HIRES error for HD 1461 in 215 selected nights
abstract: We test the disputed HD 1461 velocity wave at 22.9 days in independent HARPS and HIRES exposures. A wave fitted to 245 HARPS nights increases weighted error in 215 HIRES nights by 4.97 percent. A HARPS-only peak at 22.917933 days also fails to reduce error. The known 13.5-day control reduces error by 17.42 percent. This does not exclude a weak orbit. With 30-day sign blocks, injection recovery is only 23 percent at the fitted 0.538 m/s amplitude and 45 percent at 0.75 m/s. A test that includes noise in both instruments gives a common-wave tail fraction of 0.0995. The result is a failure to confirm a known disputed signal, not a new planet claim. Fixed noise scales, block assumptions, circular waves and common stellar activity limit the test. Code, input hashes, aggregate results and retrieval steps are included. External source records are excluded.
